text:
customer_jane: Hey team — since this morning our Private deploy to staging is getting intermittent 502s from the KMS path when calling Redwood API: `POST /v1/keys/:key:encrypt`. Error in logs: `tls: handshake timeout` and `read tcp ...: read: connection reset by peer`. Started ~08:12 UTC after we rolled a new cert on our HSM appliance. Request IDs: req-0a1b2c3d. Any ideas?
eli_support: Sorry you're hit — can you paste the client-side TLS logs and a quick curl repro? Also confirm if this is only from one VPC/subnet or all hosts behind the NAT gateway.
customer_jane: Repro from one app host (10.0.5.12) attached. Quick curl shows: `curl -v https://kms.private.example.com/health` -> hangs and then `* Failed to connect to kms.private.example.com port 443: Connection timed out` and sometimes `Connection reset by peer`.
eli_support: Can you run `openssl s_client -connect kms.private.example.com:443 -servername kms.private.example.com -showcerts` from the same host and paste output? Also try `dig +short kms.private.example.com` to see DNS resolution.
customer_jane: Dig shows multiple A records: `10.20.1.5` `10.20.1.6` `10.20.1.7`. OpenSSL output shows first attempt returns the new cert (CN=kms.private.example.com) but 2/5 attempts fail with `handshake timed out`. When it succeeds, cert is valid.
ivan_infra: @customer_jane quick hypothesis: after cert rotation the HSM front-door LB started returning multiple backend IPs that are in a different AZ and require SNAT for return path. If clients open lots of short-lived TLS connections to many backend IPs, ephemeral port exhaustion + asymmetric SNAT can cause `connection reset` / handshake timeouts.
ryan_ops: Also check that your egress allowlist on the firewall permits all backend IPs the FQDN resolves to. If the firewall only allowed the previous single IP, traffic to rotated IPs would be blocked intermittently.
customer_jane: We only added the fqdn to the allowlist (the security team asked for hostnames only). Our egress proxy does DNS->IP mapping and only permits the first IP returned by our internal resolver. Looks like rotation shuffled the order.
eli_support: Quick repro step: on the app host, try `curl --resolve kms.private.example.com:443:10.20.1.5 https://kms.private.example.com/health -v` and then the same with `10.20.1.6` and `10.20.1.7`. If one of them works consistently and others fail, that shows backend-specific connectivity issue / allowlist gap.
customer_jane: Ran the --resolve tests: 10.20.1.5 => success, 10.20.1.6 => TLS handshake timeout, 10.20.1.7 => reset.
ivan_infra: That confirms multiple backend paths. Two immediate mitigations: 1) add the full set of backend IPs to your egress allowlist (or allow the CIDR the HSM sits in) so rotated IPs aren't blocked, 2) enable connection pooling/pinned connections to reduce ephemeral ports and SNAT churn.
ryan_ops: Long-term fix: ask the HSM team to advertise a stable VIP or use an internal LB that preserves source IP, or update the NAT gateway to use larger port range / multiple SNATs to avoid exhaustion. Also consider health-checking all IPs and prefer healthy ones.
customer_jane: Security team reluctant to open CIDR, wants to keep hostname-based allowlist. Any way to make hostname-only policy reliable with rotating A records?
eli_support: Hostname-based allowlist is brittle when the resolver returns different IPs. Options: - allow the target CIDR/pool in firewall, - maintain an automated job to resolve FQDN regularly and sync IPs to allowlist, or - route KMS traffic through a dedicated egress ENI with a stable IP that the HSM can allowlist.
ivan_infra: Another quick check: can you run `ss -tanp | grep 443` and `cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | grep 10.20.1` during repro to see if conntrack entries hit limits? If conntrack table is full you'll see failures.
customer_jane: Dumped conntrack: it's near capacity on the NAT host. Looks like many TIME_WAIT entries from transient TLS connections.
ryan_ops: That aligns with SNAT port exhaustion theory. For immediate relief: increase ephemeral port range on NAT host and shorten TIME_WAIT with `tcp_tw_reuse`/`tcp_fin_timeout` tweaks where allowed. Also throttle client connection churn.
eli_support: Also confirm TLS SNI is set correctly in the KMS client (some older SDKs set SNI to internal-hostname or IP, which can cause the server to present a wrong cert). You mentioned a cert rotation — if some backends still expect old SNI name, they might close the handshake.
customer_jane: Confirmed our SDK sets SNI correctly to `kms.private.example.com`.
infra-bot: cert-rotation job completed at 1812345800, rotated cert bundle and updated intermediate CA chain.
ivan_infra: Given the cert rotation coincided with new backend IPs, sequence likely: rotation triggered deployment that changed backend pool -> DNS results changed -> client-side allowlist + SNAT issues -> intermittent failures.
eli_support: Action items: 1) customer: add all resolved IPs or CIDR to allowlist and increase conntrack/ephemeral port range (temporary), 2) infra: talk to HSM LB team to provide stable VIP or document IP ranges, 3) ops: consider dedicated egress ENI for KMS traffic. I'll open a support case with priority P1 and link logs.
customer_jane: Thanks — we'll open change to push the full CIDR to security and schedule a follow-up. Please attach SRE recommendations for conntrack tuning.
eli_support: Case created: RINF-73921. Tagging @ryan_ops @ivan_infra. We'll follow up after your security change. :thumbsup:
customer_jane: Appreciate it. I'll update here once firewall change is live. :pray:
